content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement to the disclosure text.

input.summary: Full ledger review completed. I traced all 16 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method) limitation by limitation, all 27 reference numerals (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 132, 134, 140, 202-216), every structure, relationship, threshold, condition, result and variant in the Field, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all four figure briefs (FIG. 1-4) including every leader destination, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. Supported and traced without exception: the branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors as an independent safety input; the isolated local bus between controller, connector interfaces and contactors; the stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value per active connector; the per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve; minimum-sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution; pilot delivery of assigned limits with connector-sensor verification; the reduced pilot command, verification interval and one-at-a-time ordered shedding in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the limit (claims 2 and 12 re-measurement follow from "one at a time ... until"); the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay; the welded-contactor leakage-threshold recording with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and the local fault indicator; the network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation, expiry-gated new sessions, and tamper-evident meter records uploaded on return; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only on sensor agreement. Numerals are one-to-one with parts, each numeral appears in exactly one consistent role across text and figures, FIG. 4 shape counts (seven rectangles plus one diamond) match the eight numbered steps and their column order, no section lines exist to designate, the abstract is within the word limit, no means-plus-function language appears, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. The generic squares, rectangles and rounded outline are shape-neutral depiction conventions confined to the figure briefs, and the application text contains no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" statement added to justify a renderer's choice. One critical defect was found: the description and the FIG. 2 brief place the connector current sensor on the isolated local bus, a connection the disclosure never makes ("A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus"), and that assertion also contradicts claim 5, which recites the bus as coupling the controller only to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors. Note for the record, not a finding: input/conversation.md ends mid-sentence at "The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but", yet the full disclosure supplies the complete offline-authorization, meter-record and service-input material, so no draft content relies on the truncated fragment.

findings.title: Isolated local bus is depicted and described as reaching the connector current sensor, a connection the disclosure does not make (and which contradicts claim 5)
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (FIG. 1 paragraph on bus 108, and FIG. 2 paragraph on channel 120); figures/FIG-2.md (bus branching paragraph); cross-check draft/09-claims.md claim 5
findings.detail: Two places in the description and one in the FIG. 2 brief assert that the isolated local bus 108 extends to the connector current sensor 124 and carries the connector current measurement. The disclosure enumerates the bus participants exhaustively and does not include the current sensors: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." In the same disclosure paragraph the connector's parts are separately enumerated as "a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier", so "connector interfaces" is the control-pilot interface, not the sensor. No affirmative passage anywhere in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage in input/conversation.md states by what path the connector current reading reaches the controller; the nearest passage is only "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor", which affirms that a coupling exists but says nothing about it being the isolated local bus. Routing the safety-relevant per-connector measurement onto the same isolated bus that carries the contactor commands is a substantive topology and signal-path assertion, not a depiction convention. The defect is also an internal inconsistency: claim 5 recites "an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels", with no sensor, so the description and FIG. 2 currently describe a bus topology broader than the one claimed.
findings.evidence: Description, FIG. 1 paragraph: "The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current reported by the connector current sensor of each connector channel." Description, FIG. 2 paragraph: "The isolated local bus 108 reaches the contactor 122, the control-pilot interface 126 and the connector current sensor 124 of the first connector channel 120, and the edge controller 106 receives over that bus the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel." figures/FIG-2.md: "Inside the rectangle it branches three ways: one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block, a second upward to the contactor outline, and a third upward, clear of the control-pilot interface block, to the lower side of the square outline of the connector current sensor." Disclosure (only bus passage): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." Claim 5: "an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels."
findings.fix: (1) In draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 1 paragraph, replace "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current reported by the connector current sensor of each connector channel" with "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports". (2) In draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph, replace "The isolated local bus 108 reaches the contactor 122, the control-pilot interface 126 and the connector current sensor 124 of the first connector channel 120, and the edge controller 106 receives over that bus the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel." with "The isolated local bus 108 reaches the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." (3) In figures/FIG-2.md, replace "Inside the rectangle it branches three ways: one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block, a second upward to the contactor outline, and a third upward, clear of the control-pilot interface block, to the lower side of the square outline of the connector current sensor." with "Inside the rectangle it branches two ways: one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and a second upward to the contactor outline." Leave the numeral list of FIG-2.md unchanged; numeral 124 continues to lead to the square outline straddling the horizontal run, and no other figure brief, numeral, or claim requires editing.
